autoAuth.digitalocean: Uses the platform SSH key; a Droplet created elsewhere needs a credential once (Advanced).
autoAuth.digitaloceanHelp: Once the DigitalOcean account is added, the platform key is an SSH key of the account, and Droplets gpuworks creates afterwards carry it. DigitalOcean cannot add an account key to an existing Droplet; for a Droplet created elsewhere, give a private key or password once under Advanced settings, and the platform key is written on sign-in.
autoAuth.aliyun: Installs as root via Cloud Assistant; no SSH credential or public IP needed.
autoAuth.aliyunHelp: GPUWorks runs the install as root through Alibaba Cloud Cloud Assistant. When Cloud Assistant is offline it falls back to SSH on the public address; give a password or key under Advanced for that.
autoAuth.runpod: Uses the platform SSH key; a Pod running from before needs it added, which restarts the Pod.
autoAuth.runpodHelp: The public key is under Settings → Nodes & deployments → SSH Key. GPUWorks adds it to your RunPod account's SSH keys when the account is added, and RunPod writes account keys into a Pod when it starts, so Pods started from then on need nothing. A Pod already running does not accept it yet: the install asks whether to change the Pod's configuration to add it (which restarts the Pod), or you can give its private key under Advanced once.
autoAuth.vast: Attaches the platform SSH key via the Vast API; nothing to enter here.
autoAuth.vastHelp: The public key is under Settings → Nodes & deployments → SSH Key.
autoAuth.compshare: Signs in once with the instance password, then uses the platform key; nothing to enter.
autoAuth.compshareHelp: CompShare instances only offer password login: GPUWorks signs in once with the password the CompShare API issued, adds its platform SSH key (public key under Settings → Nodes & deployments → SSH Key), and uses the key from then on.
autoAuth.autodl: Signs in once with AutoDL's root password, then uses the platform key; nothing to enter.
autoAuth.autodlHelp: GPUWorks signs in once with the root password AutoDL issued for the instance, adds its platform SSH key (public key under Settings → Nodes & deployments → SSH Key), and uses the key from then on.
autoAuth.other: Uses the platform SSH key; if the instance does not accept it, give a credential under Advanced.
autoAuth.otherHelp: The public key is under Settings → Nodes & deployments → SSH Key. If the instance does not accept it yet, give a private key or password under Advanced once; the key is added during the install.

install.credentialOverrideHelp: Only needed when the GPUWorks platform key and the external platform's own login do not work. After a successful login the GPUWorks platform key is added and these are not kept.
install.running: Installing the agent. This can take up to a minute; the result appears here.

installed.title: Agent installed and connected
installed.description: The agent is running and has connected to this server. The instance now shows as onboarded and the node appears under Compute Nodes.

installedWithNotes.title: Agent installed, with notes
installedWithNotes.description: The agent was installed. The items marked Warning or Failed below are worth a look, but the install itself went through.

waitingForAgent.title: Agent started, not connected yet
waitingForAgent.description: The agent is running on the instance but has not connected to this server yet. Check Compute Nodes in a minute. If it never appears, the server address is probably not reachable from the instance; see the agent_dial row below.

waitingForServer.title: Agent started, the server cannot reach it yet
waitingForServer.description: The agent is running on the instance, but the server cannot connect to its port yet, usually because a security group or firewall blocks it: see the server_dial row below and the precheck details. Once the port is open the server connects on its own; no need to install again.

failed.title: Installation failed
failed.description: The agent was not installed. See the checks below for the reason.

install.title: Install Agent · {{name}}
install.passwordPlaceholder: SSH password (used when no private key is supplied, such as password-only cloud hosts)
install.agentAddressHelp: The address the server connects to this instance at. With a host only, the port is the listen port; when the external platform maps the port to another number, give the mapped address and port.
install.autodlAgentDialOnly: The AutoDL one-click install supports agent-initiated connections only. For a server-initiated connection, follow
install.autodlPortDocs: the AutoDL documentation to open a TCP port, then add the node by hand under Add compute node
install.autoPortHelp: With both left empty, a TCP port the instance maps and nothing holds is used, and the address filled in.

restartConfirm.title: Restart the pod?
restartConfirm.content: RunPod opens a port only by changing the pod's configuration, which restarts its container and clears what is not on a volume. Add the port automatically?
restartConfirm.contentSSHKey: This pod started before the GPUWorks platform key was added to the RunPod account, so it does not accept the key yet. RunPod adds a key only by changing the pod's configuration, which restarts its container and clears what is not on a volume. Add it automatically?
restartConfirm.contentSSHKeyPort: This pod does not accept the GPUWorks platform key yet and has no TCP port to use. RunPod adds a key and opens a port only by changing the pod's configuration, which restarts its container and clears what is not on a volume. Add both automatically?

install.installDirHelp: Holds the agent, models and runtime data; empty means /opt/gpuworks. Give an absolute path starting with /, such as /data/gpuworks on a data disk; the install fails when a directory given here cannot be written.
install.useSystemdHelp: On: the agent is registered as the gpuworks-agent systemd service, started at boot and restarted when it crashes; instances without systemd (most container instances) always run it under nohup.
install.useSystemdOffHelp: The agent runs under nohup: it does not start at boot and is not restarted when it exits; the host's existing gpuworks-agent service and agents in other directories are left alone.
install.listenAddressHelp: Where the agent listens on the instance (or in its container): its --listen.
install.attemptFailed: Connection to {{target}} failed; fell back automatically

clusters.empty: This account has no managed Kubernetes clusters
clusters.entryGone: The account no longer has this cluster. Its entry and the nodes that joined are still here: revoke or delete it on the right.
clusters.entryUnread: The cloud's clusters could not be read, so the node pools cannot be shown; the entry can still be managed on the right.
clusters.privateAPIHint: The API server has no public address, so gpuworks cannot apply the manifest for you; after connecting, run the kubectl command from inside the cluster's network.
clusters.noGPUPools: No recognizable GPU node pool (auto-mode pools, shared GPUs and unsupported vendors are not listed)
